subject: Packing the Plan: composable feature matrix & downgrade safeguards
messages:
From: Lena Alvarez <lena@bluecrest.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: owen.park@bluecrest.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Composable plan mapping + downgrade questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput numbers. We're trying to decide how to structure our contract and wanted to check a few packaging/ops details before we take the next step:

- We plan to use embeddings at scale for semantic search (heavy) plus occasional chat endpoints for internal tooling (spiky). Which plan(s) best map to that mix?
- How do feature bundles behave when you upgrade/downgrade? For example, if we move from a mid-tier to a lower tier after 6 months, do we lose prepay credits or feature entitlements immediately?
- Are there explicit quotas tied to model families (e.g., can we pin a hosted model and still use caching benefits if we downgrade)?

I've attached a quick usage export (current_usage_report.csv) so you can see our token/embedding split. We're also evaluating Dedicated later this year and want to understand safe downgrade paths and any crediting that preserves our work.

Can we run a short 30-min packaging review this week? Owen (copied) will handle SRE/infra questions.

Appreciate any quick guidance — happy to share more detail in the call.

Thanks,
Lena Alvarez
Head of Procurement | BlueCrest AI

Attachments: current_usage_report.csv (text/csv)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Lena Alvarez <lena@bluecrest.ai>, Owen Park <owen.park@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Composable plan mapping + downgrade questions

Hi Lena / Owen,

Thanks for the usage file — that helps. High-level answers up front:

- For a mixed workload (heavy embeddings + spiky chat), we typically recommend a composable approach: base Hosted plan for embeddings with an add-on seat for chat throughput, or Dedicated for embeddings if sustained throughput is above ~5M embeddings/month.
- Downgrades: entitlements (features like priority routing, long-term KV cache retention, and advanced batching) are policy-based. If you downgrade to a lower tier, you lose access to tiered features immediately but we roll remaining prepaid tokens into a prorated credit that you can apply to a 30-day grace period while you migrate.
- Model pinning: you can pin model variants (within our catalog) and keep caching benefits for compatible runtime variants. If you switch to a model that is not supported in the lower tier, the platform will route to the most compatible supported variant (with notification).

I'm attaching a first-pass packaging matrix (packaging_matrix_v1.xlsx) that maps your usage buckets to our plan constructs and flags downgrade risk areas. Quick ask: can you confirm whether your embeddings traffic uses 1536-dimension vectors or a custom size? That changes the cost buckets.

I propose a 30-min workshop tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to walk the matrix and agree on a safe downgrade policy and credits. If that works, Marissa from SE and Monica from CS will join to cover performance tradeoffs and migration steps.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: packaging_matrix_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lena Alvarez <lena@bluecrest.ai>, Owen Park <owen.park@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Composable plan mapping + downgrade questions

Hi Lena/Owen — quick technical note to supplement Karthik: 

- If embeddings are your primary cost driver and sustained QPS is < 300 r/s, Hosted + embedding add-on is usually the lowest friction. For sustained QPS > 300 r/s we recommend Dedicated pools with configured autoscaling.
- Downgrade mechanics: we use token-based credits. Example: if you prepay for 1M embedding units and downgrade after using 400k, the remaining 600k become a prorated credit at the new list price and are available for 30 days. We also offer a one-time migration credit for switching from Hosted to Dedicated to smooth the move.
- Feature bundling: certain features (long-term KV cache retention beyond 7 days, per-route tracing with 12-month retention, SLA-backed latency tiers) are only available on mid/high tiers. We can scope a custom add-on for retention if you need it on a lower tier.

Operational suggestion: during the first 60 days post-deployment we recommend enabling prefix caching and a read-only canary route to validate behavior; that makes rollback simpler and reduces the risk of data loss during plan changes.

I can detail the downgrade math in the workshop — happy to run a few scenarios with your usage file.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Lena Alvarez <lena@bluecrest.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, Owen Park <owen.park@bluecrest.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Composable plan mapping + downgrade questions

Karthik / Marissa — this is perfect, thanks. 10:00 AM PT tomorrow works for us. We'll share the embedding dimension and a slightly larger export ahead of the call.

Two asks to prep the proposal:
1) Can you include the explicit downgrade example with numbers (prepay -> prorated credit -> apply to lower-tier usage) so our finance team can model the P&L?
2) Any standard discount bands for 12-month vs 24-month commitments and how they interact with credits? We're particularly interested in the range and whether the discount is applied before or after a downgrade credit.

If you can drop a short PDF with the downgrade policy (redwood_downgrade_policy.pdf) and a bullet summary of discount mechanics before the call that would help speed approvals.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Alvarez
Head of Procurement | BlueCrest AI
